senses.definition: a marker (as of ribbon, leather, or paper) inserted between pages of a book
examples: She slipped a ribbon bookmark into the page.

senses.definition: a record of the address of a file or webpage on the internet, enabling quick access
examples: He added the documentation link to his browser bookmarks.

senses.definition: record the address of a website, file, or page to enable quick access in future
examples: Don't forget to bookmark this useful repository.

senses.definition: a reference book or online resource containing an alphabetical list of words, with information given for each word including meaning, pronunciation, etymology, and usage
examples: I looked up the rare term in the unabridged dictionary.

senses.definition: a sturdy table at which manual work or software development is done
examples: The engineer kept all key environment tools arranged neatly on the workbench.

senses.definition: a person or item that organizes things, files, or information efficiently
examples: Bookmark Organizer keeps your projects organized across workspaces.

senses.definition: try to find something by looking or otherwise seeking carefully and thoroughly
examples: Use Spotlight search to instantly locate environments and documentation.

senses.definition: an act of searching for someone or something
examples: The quick search returned exact results across all active categories.

senses.definition: the principal method of human communication, consisting of words used in a structured and conventional way
examples: The dictionary module supports multiple languages including Japanese and English.

senses.definition: an electronic device for storing and processing data, typically in binary form
examples: The application operates entirely locally on your personal computer.

senses.definition: the programs and other operating information used by a computer
examples: Reliable open source software respects user privacy and data ownership.

senses.definition: a group or system of interconnected people or things, or connected computers
examples: The offline dictionary requires zero network connection once installed.

senses.definition: the surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives, or the software context (DEV, TEST, PROD)
examples: Switch seamlessly between DEV, TEST, and PROD portals.

senses.definition: a computer program with a graphical user interface for displaying and navigating between web pages
examples: The extension works across Chrome, Firefox, and Chromium-based browsers.

senses.definition: facts, information, and skills acquired by a person through experience or education
examples: The dictionary provides verified linguistic knowledge.

senses.definition: the systematic study of the structure and behavior of the physical and natural world through observation and experiment
examples: Computer science principles guide efficient indexing algorithms.

senses.definition: making little or no noise; peaceful, unobtrusive
examples: A quiet digital workbench avoids noisy notifications and unwanted popups.

senses.definition: the state or condition of being free from being observed or disturbed by other people, tracking, or telemetry
examples: Zero tracking and strictly local storage guarantee complete user privacy.

senses.definition: a single distinct meaningful element of speech or writing, used with others to form a sentence
examples: Look up any unfamiliar word in the built-in offline dictionary.

senses.definition: what is meant by a word, text, concept, or action
examples: The dictionary explains the subtle meaning of each sense.

senses.definition: the circumstances that form the setting for an event, statement, or idea, and in terms of which it can be fully understood
examples: AI explains the exact nuance of the word within the context of the sentence.

senses.definition: the power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without hindrance or restraint
examples: Open source software grants users the freedom to inspect and control their tools.

senses.definition: freedom from disturbance; tranquility, serenity, harmony
examples: A calm interface brings peace of mind to daily web browsing.
